# Reading Ḥr the way it was meant to be written
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Ḥr** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Horus's mythology is the political theology of Egypt made personal. It tells how the rightful heir, born from a murdered father and a resourceful mother, defeats the usurper and restores the throne. The story was never merely entertainment; it was the charter of kingship, replayed in temples for three thousand years. Horus the Elder (Haroeris) is an ancient sky-god, brother of Osiris and Set, whose eyes are the luminaries.  Horus the Younger (Harsiese) is the son of Osiris and Isis, the avenger of his father.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ḥr
- **ASCII form:** horus
- **Meaning:** "The Distant One (Egyptian ḥr)"
- **Domain of influence:** Sky, Kingship, Falcon
- **Pantheon:** Egyptian
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 𓅃
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 109 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Ḥr** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *horus* and **Ḥr** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ḥr** lives at [/sites/horus/](/sites/horus/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/horus/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/horus/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/horus/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Ḥr** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Leadership, Governance & Public Administration** — Kingship itself; every pharaoh ruled as the living Horus.
- **Aviation & Aerospace** — The falcon of the sky; the falcon remains aviation’s favorite emblem.
- **Optics, Imaging & Vision** — The Eye of Horus; the most famous protective eye in history.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Egyptian tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [The Book of the Dead](/texts/book-of-the-dead/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
